skill.name: email-quality-auditor
skill.description: Audits an email program against 20 SEND criteria covering sender integrity, engagement, nurture, direct outcomes, consent, suppression, and claims.
skill.summary: Assess email readiness with evidence-based scoring, veto checks, and clear release guidance.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, metadata URLs, fixed documentation links, or a controlled Git command without user-controlled arguments. The direct instruction to read parent-directory references crosses the packaged skill boundary and remains a confirmed filesystem concern.

remediation.issue: The runtime setup directs the agent to read references outside the packaged skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use only bundled references in standalone installs, and resolve repository references through a verified root without parent-directory traversal.

content.value_statement: Email programs can hide authentication, consent, suppression, engagement, and claim risks. This skill evaluates 20 SEND criteria and reports evidence gaps, vetoes, and release guidance.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates 20 criteria across sender integrity, engagement, nurture, and direct outcomes.
Checks authentication, consent provenance, opt-out handling, suppression state, and material claims.
Separates measured outcomes from provider metrics and MPP-sensitive open data.
Assigns explicit pass, partial, fail, unknown, or not-applicable states to each criterion.
Reports release guidance, evidence gaps, confidence, critical controls, and responsible fix owners.
limitations: Requires current evidence from providers, DNS, consent records, rendered messages, and outcome systems.
Does not send email or change provider, consent, suppression, or claim settings.
Cannot produce a comparable score when required evidence remains unknown.
Standalone installs provide observations only and cannot issue a final gate verdict.

use_cases.title: Approve a Newsletter Release
use_cases.description: Review authentication, subscription records, suppressions, engagement evidence, and claims before a scheduled newsletter.

use_cases.title: Investigate Program Quality
use_cases.description: Compare provider cohorts, MPP share, complaints, frequency, lifecycle controls, and verified outcomes across a defined observation window.

use_cases.title: Document Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Record consent provenance, one-click opt-out behavior, live suppression handling, and approved claim evidence for a campaign review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Campaign Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this newsletter before release. List the evidence you need and identify any immediate blockers from the material I provide.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured pre-send review.

prompt_templates.title: Score an Email Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this promotional program using the SEND framework. Use the last 90 days and mark missing evidence as unknown.
prompt_templates.scenario: A campaign owner has provider exports and campaign materials.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Providers and Outcomes
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this retention program by provider and cohort. Separate MPP-sensitive metrics from clicks, downstream actions, and the declared outcome truth set.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs a defensible quality assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Advanced Gate Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate all 20 SEND criteria for this cold-outbound program. Verify veto controls, explain confidence, report unknowns, and assign fix owners.
prompt_templates.scenario: A senior reviewer needs a complete release decision.

output_examples.input: Audit a newsletter with complete evidence, a score of 81, and no failed veto controls.
output_examples.output: Verdict: Ship. The program scored 81 with complete coverage and no verified veto failures. Continue monitoring provider placement and direct outcomes.

output_examples.input: Audit a promotional send with missing consent provenance and incomplete suppression evidence.
output_examples.output: Verdict: Undecided. Consent and suppression controls remain unknown, so no comparable score or release approval is available. Supply current records before sending.

output_examples.input: Audit a program with a verified unlawful list and a broken opt-out process.
output_examples.output: Verdict: Block. Two critical veto controls failed. Stop the send, remove unlawful recipients, repair opt-out handling, and verify live suppressions.

best_practices: Provide dated evidence for one declared program, provider scope, market, and normalized observation window.
Use clicks and downstream actions as primary engagement evidence when available.
Verify live consent and suppression state before requesting a release verdict.
anti_patterns: Do not treat missing records as passing evidence or as not applicable.
Do not infer inbox placement from DNS authentication alone.
Do not use open rate or CTOR as proof of human attention without MPP caveats.

faq.question: What evidence does the audit require?
faq.answer: Provide provider exports, DNS or header evidence, consent events, live suppressions, rendered messages, and a declared outcome truth set.

faq.question: Does the skill send or modify email?
faq.answer: No. It reviews evidence and reports findings without sending messages or changing provider settings.

faq.question: What email programs are supported?
faq.answer: The profiles are promotional, retention, cold outbound, and newsletter.

faq.question: How are missing records handled?
faq.answer: Applicable but missing evidence is marked unknown. Unknown controls can prevent a score or gate verdict.

faq.question: Can open rate prove engagement?
faq.answer: No. Open rate is an MPP-sensitive proxy and needs segmentation and a clear caveat.

faq.question: What can block a send?
faq.answer: Verified authentication failure, unlawful list use, broken opt-out handling, or unsupported material claims can trigger vetoes.
